title: Daemon MCP host: wire boundSessionIds() or remove it
description:
A DOCUMENTED SURFACE WITH ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS. Raised by worker-40286572 during the close-out of the audit register, deliberately left out of task-70b6361d, and filed here so it is not dropped the way register item 5's second clause was.

apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-session-port.ts:60-67 declares, on McpHttpSessionPort:

    /**
     * Transport session ids currently bound, in bind order. Real production surface: the host
     * closes outstanding sessions on shutdown and cannot do that without asking.
     */
    boundSessionIds(): readonly string[];

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 181e0e9, not quoted from the original report: `grep -rn boundSessionIds --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns exactly FOUR hits — the interface declaration at mcp-http-session-port.ts:65, its implementation at :104, and two assertions in its own mcp-http-session-port.test.ts:284 and :288. No production caller anywhere. The comment states an obligation the codebase does not discharge.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER IT, and why this is now a decision rather than a gap. task-70b6361d (commit 181e0e9) made the ADAPTER release every daemon-side binding at shutdown: createHttpMcpAdapter().close() now sweeps its whole registry through closeDaemonSession, so options.sessionPort.closeSession fires once per session still open. apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts doStop() (:203-215) already awaits adapter.close(), so the host's outstanding sessions ARE now closed on shutdown — by the adapter, without the host ever asking. That is what makes the accessor's stated reason for existing obsolete rather than merely unimplemented.

THE TWO HONEST OUTCOMES, and this task must pick one on measurement rather than taste:
(a) REMOVE boundSessionIds() from the interface, from the implementation, and its two test assertions, and delete the comment claiming the host needs it. Justified if the adapter sweep is genuinely sufficient — which is the reading task-70b6361d's evidence supports.
(b) WIRE IT, if and only if a case exists where the host holds a binding the adapter's registry does not: e.g. a session bound daemon-side whose adapter registration failed, or an adapter replaced without close(). If such a case is found, name it concretely and add the host-side sweep with a test that reddens when it is removed.

DO NOT re-implement the adapter sweep in the host as a belt-and-braces second release. A doubly-released session is a different defect, not a stricter fix — task-70b6361d's DoD 3 pins exactly-once and its test asserts it.

Hard dependencies: MCP adapter close must release daemon-side session bindings (task-70b6361d94094db48b15d32eb8e4b931, DONE at commit 181e0e9). Its outcome is the premise for choosing (a) over (b), so this task cannot be planned before reading that commit.

Scope: apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/** only. packages/mcp is finished and owned by the prerequisite; do not reopen it.
definitionOfDone: The measurement is redone at the then-current HEAD before any edit and recorded symbol by symbol: `grep -rn boundSessionIds --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` with its full hit list, and whether mcp-http-host.ts still awaits adapter.close() in doStop(). A claim inherited from this description rather than re-measured does not satisfy this.

Outcome (a) or (b) is chosen and the reasoning written down, naming the concrete case that decides it. If (b), that case is reproduced as a failing test BEFORE the wiring lands; if (a), the accessor, its implementation, its two test assertions and the comment claiming the host needs it are all removed together — leaving the comment behind would recreate the exact defect this task exists to close.

No session can be released twice. If (b) is chosen, a test opens sessions through the real adapter, drives host shutdown, and asserts each session's closeSession was observed EXACTLY once — not merely at least once. The adapter already releases them, so an unguarded host sweep is a double release.

Any refusal or failure path added carries a stable reason code and names its layer, asserted by a test that pins the code itself rather than merely that the operation did not succeed - epic rail 4 and the reason-code rail.

Every assertion added or changed is proven load-bearing by a mutation drill: mutate the production surface, confirm a NAMED test goes red on the assertion the drill targets, restore, and verify the restore by sha256 rather than by `git diff` - the shared worktree makes an untracked file invisible to diff.

Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exits 0, with each leg's exit code read separately, and the pre-existing mcp-http-session-port.test.ts and mcp-http-host.test.ts cases outside this change still pass unchanged.
taskRails: Scope is apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/** only. packages/mcp/src/http/** is finished and owned by the prerequisite task; a fix that reaches back into the adapter is out of scope and collides with landed code in this shared worktree.

Do not add a second release path over the same sessions. The adapter already releases every binding it holds at close(); a host sweep layered on top of it is a double release, which is a different defect and not a stricter fix.

Removal is a legitimate outcome and is not a coverage regression. If the accessor goes, its two test assertions go with it and the docstring claiming the host needs it goes too - a comment left behind restates the discharged-obligation defect that produced the prerequisite task.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source, split before 400. Measure mcp-http-session-port.ts and mcp-http-host.ts with `grep -c ''` before adding to either.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE AT THE THEN-CURRENT HEAD BEFORE ANY EDIT, and record every command with its full output (DoD 1). Nothing is edited in this step.

CRITICAL READ DISCIPLINE: a peer is running mutation drills in packages/mcp in this shared worktree — that file changed twice under the architect during planning. Read every packages/mcp premise via `git show HEAD:<path>`, NEVER `cat`. The working tree there is not evidence.

Commands:
1. `git rev-parse --short HEAD` — record it; the plan's premise was measured at 181e0e9.
2. `grep -rn boundSessionIds --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` — record the FULL hit list. Expected: exactly four (mcp-http-session-port.ts:65 declaration, :104 implementation, mcp-http-session-port.test.ts:284 and :288).
3. `git show HEAD:apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts | grep -n "doStop\|open.close()\|adapter = null"` — record whether doStop() still awaits adapter.close(). Expected: doStop :203, `adapter = null` :210, `await open.close()` :214.
4. `git show HEAD:packages/mcp/src/http/http-shutdown.ts | grep -n closeDaemonSession` — record whether the adapter sweep still routes the daemon release through closeDaemonSession. Expected: a call at :104 inside closeAllDaemonSessions.
5. `grep -c ''` on mcp-http-session-port.ts and mcp-http-host.ts for the line budget (expected 114 and 222).

STOP CONDITION: if the hit list is no longer exactly four, or ANY production caller of boundSessionIds has appeared, or the adapter no longer calls closeDaemonSession, the decision premise has changed — do not proceed. Call moe.report_blocked quoting the new measurement.

WRITE THE DECISION DOWN, naming the concrete case that decides it (DoD 2). No code edit — this is the recorded reasoning that DoD 2 requires, and it must be reproduced in the completion notes.

CHOSEN: outcome (a) REMOVE. The three candidate (b) cases the task names were each refuted by measurement:

(b1) 'an adapter replaced without close()'. REFUTED: adapterOf() is `adapter ??= createHttpMcpAdapter(...)`, which assigns only when null, and the sole path to null is doStop(), which captures `open = adapter` before nulling and always awaits `open.close()`. No path replaces a live adapter unclosed.

(b2) 'a session bound daemon-side whose adapter registration failed'. REFUTED as actionable: bindDaemonSession does `await port.bindSession(...)` then `registry.bind(...)`, so the orphan window is a throw strictly between two Map.set calls; and the remedy would live in packages/mcp, which task rail 1 puts out of scope.

(b3) 'an initialize completing after close()'s entries() snapshot' — the residual risk the prerequisite disclosed. REAL, and it is the case that settles the task, because it is inconsequential HERE: the session port is constructed INLINE at mcp-http-host.ts:137 inside adapterOf() and the host stores no reference to it, so the port and its `bound` map are dropped together when doStop() sets `adapter = null`. The map is, in the port's own words at :70, 'in-process routing state, never durable identity' — an unswept entry outlives nothing.

DECIDING FACT: the host holds NO reference to the session port. The docstring's claim — 'the host closes outstanding sessions on shutdown and cannot do that without asking' — is false in both clauses: the adapter closes them, and the host has nothing to ask. Wiring (b) would first require hoisting the port into a host-level variable, creating the coupling the docstring asserts already exists in order to justify the accessor asserting it. Circular.

Also record here, so it is not invented later: outcome (a) adds NO refusal or failure path, so DoD 4 has no reason code to pin. State that as the finding.
implementationPlan.note:
DECISION RECORDED (DoD 2). No code edit. Each (b) candidate re-verified by me at HEAD 181e0e9, not inherited from the plan.

CHOSEN: OUTCOME (a) — REMOVE boundSessionIds(), its implementation, its two test assertions, and the docstring claiming the host needs it.

(b1) "an adapter replaced without close()" — REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. `git show HEAD:apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.ts` :125-127 is `adapter ??= createHttpMcpAdapter({...})` — `??=` assigns only when the field is null. The sole path to null is doStop() (:203-215), which does `const open = adapter;` then `adapter = null;` then `if (open !== null) await open.close();`. No code path replaces a live adapter without closing it, so no adapter can be discarded holding unreleased bindings.

(b2) "a session bound daemon-side whose adapter registration failed" — REFUTED AS ACTIONABLE. `git show HEAD:packages/mcp/src/http/http-session.ts` :202-211: bindDaemonSession is `await port.bindSession(mcpSessionId, verdict);` then `registry.bind(mcpSessionId, verdict, attachment);`. The orphan window is a throw strictly between two Map.set calls. Even granting it, the remedy lives in packages/mcp, which task rail 1 places out of scope and the prerequisite owns.

(b3) "an initialize completing after close()'s entries() snapshot" — REAL (the prerequisite disclosed it itself) but INCONSEQUENTIAL HERE, and it is the case that SETTLES the task. Measured: `grep -rn "McpHttpSessionPort\|createMcpHttpSessionPort" --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` shows the port's ONLY production construction is mcp-http-host.ts:137, INLINE inside adapterOf() as `sessionPort: createMcpHttpSessionPort(options.deps.authenticator),`. The host stores no reference to it. So the port instance's lifetime is exactly the adapter's, and doStop()'s `adapter = null` drops the port and its `bound` Map together. The map is, in the port's own comment at :70, "in-process routing state, never durable identity" — an unswept entry outlives nothing and costs nothing.

DECIDING FACT: THE HOST HOLDS NO REFERENCE TO THE SESSION PORT. The docstring at :61-64 — "the host closes outstanding sessions on shutdown and cannot do that without asking" — is FALSE IN BOTH CLAUSES: (i) the host does not close them, the adapter does, via closeAllDaemonSessions -> closeDaemonSession -> port.closeSession (verified at http-shutdown.ts:104 and http-session.ts:217-224 at HEAD); (ii) the host has nothing to ask, holding no port reference. Wiring (b) would first require hoisting the port into a host-level variable — i.e. CREATING the coupling the docstring claims already exists, in order to justify the accessor that claims it. Circular. An unused method deleted is honest; an unused method kept with a false guarantee is not.

DoD 4 FINDING, recorded now so it is not invented later: outcome (a) adds NO refusal or failure path — it is a pure deletion of an accessor plus a comment. There is therefore NO reason code to pin and no layer to name. DoD 4 is satisfied vacuously and honestly. I will not invent a code in order to have one.

DoD 3 FINDING: outcome (a) adds no release path at all, so no session can be released twice by construction. The adapter remains the sole releaser. Step 7 check 1 re-verifies this by grep.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
OUTCOME (b) WIRE was evaluated against all three concrete cases the task names, and each was refuted BY MEASUREMENT at HEAD 181e0e9, not by taste.

(b1) 'an adapter replaced without close()'. REFUTED. mcp-http-host.ts adapterOf() is `adapter ??= createHttpMcpAdapter(...)` — it assigns only when the field is null. The only path that sets it null is doStop() (:203-215), which captures `open = adapter` BEFORE nulling and then `await open.close()` at :214. No code path replaces a live adapter without closing it.

(b2) 'a session bound daemon-side whose adapter registration failed'. REFUTED as actionable. bindDaemonSession (packages/mcp http-session.ts:202-211) is `await port.bindSession(...)` then `registry.bind(...)`; the orphan window is a throw strictly between two Map.set calls. Even granting it, the remedy lives in packages/mcp, which task rail 1 places out of scope and the prerequisite owns.

(b3) 'an initialize completing after close()'s snapshot' — the residual risk task-70b6361d disclosed itself. REAL but INCONSEQUENTIAL HERE, and this is the case that settles the task.

THE DECIDING FACT. The session port is constructed INLINE at mcp-http-host.ts:137 — `sessionPort: createMcpHttpSessionPort(options.deps.authenticator)` — inside adapterOf(). The host stores no reference to it. grep confirms mcp-http-host.ts:137 is the only production construction site and there is no variable. So the port instance's lifetime is exactly the adapter's, and doStop()'s `adapter = null` drops the port and its `bound` Map together. The port's own comment (:70) already states the map is 'in-process routing state, never durable identity', so an unswept entry outlives nothing and costs nothing.

That makes the accessor's docstring false in BOTH of its clauses: the host does NOT close outstanding sessions on shutdown (the adapter does, via closeAllDaemonSessions -> closeDaemonSession -> port.closeSession), and the host has nothing to ask because it holds no port reference. Wiring (b) would first require hoisting the port into a host-level variable — i.e. CREATING the coupling the docstring claims already exists, in order to justify the accessor that claims it. Circular. Outcome (a) REMOVE.

The prerequisite's own author reached the same conclusion independently: its handoff memory records 'the host's doStop() already gets its sessions released by adapter.close(), so that task is a decision (remove vs wire), not a gap. Do not add a host-side sweep on top — that is a double release.'

GOING ONE STEP FURTHER THAN DoD 2 (step 4, deliberately separable). Removing the accessor leaves `bound` written by bindSession/closeSession and READ BY NOTHING — the accessor was its only reader, so after removal it is unread by construction, a static proof rather than a coverage claim. A write-only map is the same defect shape this task exists to close, one level down, and its two surviving comments ('never appends', 'no counter can drift') imply an observer that no longer exists. DoD 2's removal list is a floor, not a ceiling. Kept as its own step so QA can accept or reject it independently of steps 1-3.
